title: Valid Word Abbreviation
summary: Determine if a string matches a given abbreviation by verifying that the abbreviation accurately represents the string through the replacement of non-adjacent, non-empty substrings with their lengths, and ensuring that the lengths do not have leading zeros.
statement: Determine if a string matches a given abbreviation by verifying that the abbreviation accurately represents the string through the replacement of non-adjacent, non-empty substrings with their lengths, and ensuring that the lengths do not have leading zeros. Also, confirm that no adjacent substrings are replaced and no empty substrings are replaced.
constraints: 1 <= word.length <= 20; word contains lowercase English letters.
1 <= abbr.length <= 10; abbr contains lowercase letters and digits; every integer token fits signed 32-bit.
A numeric token skips that many letters. It must be positive and have no leading zero. The entire word must be consumed.
hints: Keep separate positions in the word and the abbreviation.
A maximal run of digits is one skip count; a letter must match the current word position.
Reject a numeric token starting with 0. Parse its full value, advance the word pointer, and reject overshoot. Require exact exhaustion at the end.
Consecutive digits represent one number, not separate adjacent replacements. This is a validity query, unlike generating all possible abbreviations.
editorial: Scan each abbreviation token once. Literal letters advance both pointers only on a match; numeric tokens advance only the word pointer. Reject zero-prefixed counts and any overshoot. Finally require the word pointer to equal the word length. The independent oracle translates tokens to a full-match pattern; exhaustive small-mask tests additionally check the semantics against enumerated valid abbreviations.

tests.explanation: Keep i, skip 12 letters, keep iz, skip 4 letters, then keep n. This consumes exactly the 20-letter word.
After a and two skipped letters, the next letter is l, not e. The valid abbreviation a3e would skip three letters instead.
